svg.text: Hover a frame for details. Click to zoom, double-click the background to reset, Ctrl+F to search.
Width = time for that operation (wider = slower). Bottom = query root; top = leaf table access.
Click a frame to zoom in on that operation. Ctrl+F to search. Hover for time, rows and loops.
Warnings below refer to specific operations by label (e.g. TABLE SCAN [users]).

materialization=on — A subquery or derived table is executed once and its result stored in a temporary table for reuse. It may spill to disk past tmp_table_size (MySQL's TempTable engine) or the smaller of tmp_table_size and max_heap_table_size (MEMORY engine, MariaDB).
1 temp table(s) (Materialize) — up to 5 rows; may spill to disk
2 sort operation(s) — 5 rows; may use disk-based filesort
• Add indexes on filter/join columns to avoid full table scans

• Check temporary-table disk usage before raising tmp_table_size together with max_heap_table_size. Why: MariaDB keeps an internal temporary table in memory only up to the smaller of the two, then converts it to an on-disk Aria or MyISAM table. A temporary table in the plan
does not by itself show that it spilled to disk.
• Increase sort_buffer_size or add an ordered index to avoid filesort
• Full scan on users with filter on (status)
• ORDER BY on users triggers a filesort; an index on the ORDER BY columns (country) lets the engine read rows already sorted, skipping the O(n log n) filesort.
⚠ Query materializes 1 temp table(s); tmp_table_size/max_heap_table_size is 16.0 MB. This limit alone does not show whether a table spilled to disk.
⚠ Table users has no index covering (status).

• Check temporary-table disk usage before increasing tmp_table_size and max_heap_table_size to the same value for this session. Why: MEMORY internal tables and MariaDB use the smaller of these two limits; exceeding it can convert a table to on-disk storage. Account for
concurrent sessions before increasing the limits.
